title: Trace Baggage and Locality Annotation Playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook describes the convention, implementation points, rollout checklist and operational runbook for: 1) propagating lightweight trace baggage across internal runtime boundaries, and 2) annotating request locality signals for fast attribution of latency and fidelity degradations. The goal is to enable sub-second triage of tail-latency and fidelity regressions with minimal telemetry cost.

Why this exists
---------------
- Traces alone are insufficient when requests traverse multiple internal runtime surfaces (dispatcher, scheduler, per-GPU worker). Baggage and locality annotations let operators reconstruct: tenant, route, model-variant, kernel-hint, and shard-affinity without expensive full-span capture.
- We must keep sampling low (<=5% overall) to control telemetry egress costs while preserving high-fidelity signals for SLO-impacting traffic.

Goals & SLO impact
------------------
- Primary goal: reduce mean time to diagnose (MTTD) tail-latency incidents from 45m to <15m for P95+ incidents caused by scheduling or kernel mis-selection.
- Maintain telemetry cost increase <= 8% on production ingestion for a 5% sampling rate.
- Do NOT degrade request latency: all baggage operations must be O(1) and performed in allocation-hot paths with preallocated buffers.

Background and design constraints
--------------------------------
1. Baggage must be compact (<= 256 bytes per request including keys), ASCII-safe, and forward-compatible.
2. Locality annotations are short enumerated codes (see schema) emitted at key transitions and attached to the trace root as tags when sampled.
3. Any new annotation must have an owner and an explicit rollout plan (below).

Telemetry schema (fields and examples)
-------------------------------------
- Field name | Type | Example | Description
-------------|------|---------|------------
- tenant_id | string | t-acme | Canonical customer id used for cost partitioning
- route | string | /v1/generate | API route or internal route name
- model_variant | string | llama2-13b-q8 | Model family + quantization/variant tag
- kernel_hint | string | shard-fused | Scheduler-provided kernel hint used for execution
- locality_code | string | W1:S3:GPU-A | Encoded placement locality (warehouse:shard:device)
- priority_tier | string | burst | Economic priority assigned by governor
- fidelity_band | string | high | Chosen fidelity slice (high/medium/low)
- kvcache_status | string | warmed | kvcache state at request arrival

Note: the table above must be represented in the telemetry backend as top-level attributes to allow fast filtering in alert dashboards.

Locality codes and decoding guide
--------------------------------
Locality codes are human-readable tokens with three components separated by colons: W{rack}:S{shard}:{device-tag}. Examples:
- W2:S7:GPU-A — warehouse 2, shard 7, device A.
- W1:S3:CPU — fallback CPU execution.
Decoding should be implemented by the runtime operator CLI (see Commands).

Sampling strategy and cost controls
----------------------------------
1. Base-sample: stratified sampling giving 5% of all requests into traces. Stratification keys: tenant_tier (enterprise/standard/free) and route.
2. Tail-preserve: conditional up-sample of requests exceeding 90th latency percentile to 25% for 30s windows around detected tail spikes. Up-sampling is gated by an egress-budget token bucket (configurable).
3. Incident-sample: on a detected SLO breach the controller can enable request-level capture for offending route/model_variant for a configurable duration (default 15m). This capture mode includes full-span traces and physiological metrics.
4. Cost cap: per-cluster daily budget enforced by telemetry-proxy; if exceeded, tail-preserve and incident-sample are disabled until replenished.

Injection points (runtime locations to attach baggage/annotations)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Frontend ingress (API gateway): attach tenant_id and route. Responsible: api-gateway service.
- Dispatcher layer: attach model_variant, priority_tier. Responsible: dispatcher-service.
- Scheduler/admission: attach kernel_hint, fidelity_band. Responsible: scheduler-service.
- Worker / GPU runtime: attach locality_code and kvcache_status (warmed/stale/empty). Responsible: worker-agent.

Implementation notes and code patterns
------------------------------------
- Use a single compact header X-RW-BAG (base64 of comma-delimited key=val pairs) for cross-process propagation. When possible, prefer binary-packed proto v1 to reduce size.
- Baggage encoding must be append-only by intermediate services; never rewrite tenant_id once set at ingress.
- Runtime helper API (pseudocode):
  - encode_baggage(map<string,string>) -> string
  - decode_baggage(string) -> map<string,string>
  - annotate_span(span, map<string,string>)
- Hot-path optimization: decoding should be lazy — decode only when the request is sampled OR when a local decision requires the field.

Runbook: Investigating a rapid P99 spike linked to kernel selection
------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Detect: Alert fired from per-route P99 > configured SLO (example: 1200ms).
2. Immediate actions (first 10 minutes):
   a. Check telemetry budget panel to ensure tail-preserve is enabled.
   b. Query the traces index for the route with attribute kernel_hint and locality_code for the offending window. Example query: "route:/v1/generate AND timestamp:[t-5m TO t] SORT BY latency DESC LIMIT 200".
   c. If traces available, aggregate by kernel_hint and locality_code. Look for a dominant kernel_hint associated with the tail.
3. Triage (10-30 minutes):
   a. If a kernel_hint shows >60% of tail samples, coordinate with kernel team to check recent kernel rollouts (see release notes index).
   b. Use worker-agent logs filtered by locality_code to inspect GPU telemetry (thermal throttling, mem fragmentation, OOM). CLI: 
      - rwi worker tail --locality=W1:S3 --since=15m 
   c. If locality shows cross-shard imbalance, escalate to scheduling team and consider transient rebalancing (see Rebalancing play).
4. Resolve (30m+):
   a. If kernel regression confirmed, trigger canary rollback following kernel rollback runbook.
   b. If kvcache coldness is root cause, engage warmup policy: increase prefix cache warmup for affected shards and enable asymmetric prefetch for the route for 2h.

Quick commands and examples
--------------------------
- Decode a baggage header locally: rwctl baggage decode --header "<base64>"
- Search traces by locality and kernel: rwctl traces query --route /v1/generate --filter "kernel_hint:shard-fused" --since 15m --limit 100
- List worker health for a locality: rwi worker list --locality W1:S3

Baggage key naming conventions
-----------------------------
- Keys MUST be lower_snake_case.
- Avoid long freeform values; prefer enumerations and short ids.
- Reserve prefix rw_* for runtime-owned keys (e.g., rw_kernel_hint).
- Example allowed keys: tenant_id, route, model_variant, rw_kernel_hint, rw_locality, kvcache_status

Security and privacy considerations
----------------------------------
- Do not propagate PII in baggage. Tenant identifiers must be opaque ids (no emails).
- Baggage header is signed by the ingress when crossing trust boundaries; internal hop-to-hop propagation is unsigned but validated for format.
- Review with legal for any new attributes that could be considered customer data.

Rollout checklist (feature flag gated)
-------------------------------------
1. Add baggage header encode/decode libs to api-gateway, dispatcher, scheduler and worker-agent. Unit tests + size regression tests.
2. Deploy library in canary region with base-sample enabled at 1%. Monitor header size distribution and egress impact for 48h.
3. Enable stratified base-sample at 5% and run for 7 days. Verify telemetry budget usage <= 8% increase.
4. Enable tail-preserve and validate tail-upsample correctness in staging with synthetic load.
5. Gradually roll to remaining regions, monitoring the telemetry budget and API latency metrics.

Safety gates and feature flags
----------------------------
- feature.runtime.baggage.enabled (bool) — global on/off
- feature.runtime.baggage.decode_lazy (bool) — lazy decode optimization
- feature.runtime.tracing.tail_preserve (bool) — enable tail up-sample
- rw.telemetry.max_daily_egress_bytes (int) — cap for cost control

Owner and escalation path
------------------------
- Primary owner: Runtime Observability (eng-serving-runtime) — Maya Patel
- Secondary owner: Kernel & Scheduler (Oliver Chen)
- Escalation: pager/runtime-sre -> oncall (see oncall roster)

--------------------------

- Kernel rollout notes: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/kernel-variant-release-log-2025

Appendix: example encoded baggage (illustrative)
------------------------------------------------
- Raw kv pairs: tenant_id=t-acme,route=/v1/generate,model_variant=llama2-13b-q8,rw_kernel_hint=shard-fused,rw_locality=W1:S3:GPU-A
- Base64 header: <base64-of-utf8-bytes-of-comma-delimited-kv>

Glossary
--------
- baggage: small cross-process key/value header propagated with requests
- locality: encoded physical/logical placement token used for fast grouping in dashboards
- tail-preserve: conditional up-sampling of tail requests to increase signal during anomalies
